task1.title: Changes in ownership of electrical appliances and time spent doing housework (1920–2019)
task1.prompt: The charts below show the changes in ownership of electrical appliances and amount of time spent doing housework in households in one country between 1920 and 2019.

chartDesc.title: Percentage of households with electrical appliances (1920–2019) / Number of hours of housework* per week, per household (1920–2019)
chartDesc.yAxis: Percentage of households / Number of hours per week
chartDesc.overview: Overall, ownership of all three electrical appliances increased over the period, with refrigerators and vacuum cleaners reaching 100% saturation, while the time spent on housework per week fell dramatically.
keyFeatures: Refrigerator ownership experienced the largest growth, starting at just around 2-3% in 1920 and reaching 100% by 1980.
Vacuum cleaner ownership rose steadily from 30% in 1920 to hit 100% in 2000.
Washing machine ownership grew from 40% in 1920 to 75% in 2019, showing a slight dip in 1980 (64%).
Housework hours decreased significantly from 50 hours per week in 1920 to 12 hours in 2019.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
